schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: THE HELP SURFACE, COMPILED FROM CHARTERS — the answer to 'what can I do here, and how', derived with zero inference. `render(charters, context) -> surface`: it walks every `intention+why.json` in class-space and projects them — a full map at the root (skills, commands, components, and the completeness verdict), or one component's whole charter when you stand in its directory (the runtime twin of Cairn's founding move: a mind is briefed by standing in a directory; a caller is briefed by asking cairnmap from one). Its proof is the DERIVATION GATE, completeness both ways: every charter'd command and skill appears, and nothing without a charter appears — an uncharted `bin/cmd/` entry or a skill absent from its roster is a RED in the map, not a missing line. `cairn cairnmap --gate` runs just that verdict with the exit code carrying it; this is the `skill` node-class's `prove_gate`, existing at last.
why: Three rulings (Akien, 2026-07-15, MAP.md 'cairnmap') fix what it is — a view, contextual, reference-only — and the 2026-07-31 session measured why it could no longer wait: MAP.md's organizing structure froze at 2026-07-14..17 while 197 commits landed in seven days, so NO ARTIFACT HELD THE DESIGN WHOLE, and Akien went 'from feeling on top of the design to feeling lost' while every piece of that week's automation (slate, trouble lane, turnscan, ruling hook) compiled CC's orientation and left his to a one-line receipt. cairnmap is the reader-side destination of MAP.md's dissolution: as the map dissolves into intentions + tickets, this renders those same records back into one surface — regenerate -> current, so it cannot drift the way the map did. A hand-written help page is the schema-apart-from-data rot that killed the quarry's docs; the compiled one is Telos 1 on the exact surface people most reflexively hand to an LLM ('explain what I can do'), with the inference compiled out. Ratified as the build for this seat 2026-07-31: 'maybe we have you do cairnmap and then we switch to opus and follow your plan.'

the_three_rulings_upheld.a_view_not_a_device: it owns no truth, only the render code. Every fact on the surface lives in a charter, the skill roster, or bin/cmd/ — all owned elsewhere (Law 6: nothing new to own). Deleting cairn/cairnmap/ loses no knowledge.
the_three_rulings_upheld.contextual_by_where: v0 scopes by WHERE: cwd inside a chartered directory -> that component's full brief; at the root -> the whole map. The next scope axis is WHO (the asker's ownership — you see only what you may invoke): designed-in, lands when the others arrive. v0 is single-user.
the_three_rulings_upheld.reference_only: it describes commands, it never runs them. The CLI mutates nothing, and render always exits 0 even when the gate inside it is red — a presentation surface may not refuse to present (Law 7's presentation half); only `--gate` carries a verdict in its exit code.

invoke: `cairn cairnmap` (the map, scoped by where you stand) · `cairn cairnmap <name|dir>` (one component's full charter) · `cairn cairnmap --gate` (the derivation gate alone: reds + verdict, exit 0 green / 1 red). Import: `from cairn.cairnmap import cairnmap`. Prove: `python3 cairn/cairnmap/proofs/test_cairnmap.py` (exit 0 = green). `CAIRN_ROOTS_PARENT` + `CAIRN_SKILLS_INSTALL_DIR` point it at a temp world for the proof.
node_class: code-seam — the render code is the code, one address. But the THING it implements is a view (per the ruling): the code is proved like any seam; the surface it emits is derived and never authored.
zero_inference_means: projection and mechanical truncation only. The one-line entries are the FIRST SENTENCE of each charter's `what` — a cut, never a paraphrase. So a confusing help line is a bug in the charter, fixed at source, never patched here: help quality ≡ charter quality, by construction, feedback landing at the point of creation.
how_it_learns: It doesn't, because it is a derivation — regenerate -> current is the whole contract, and a view that accumulated its own state would be a second owner of the truth it renders (Law 6). What learns is the charter corpus underneath it: every red this gate raises is fixed in a charter, a roster, or a command's coverage, and the next render inherits the fix for free.
entry: FRESH build 2026-07-31. In-house precedent, cited not copied: bin/cmd/slate (a compiled projection of records, read every session; the proof-over-live-data discipline of injectable roots), bin's charter `flight_recorder` block (the resident-facility shape the command-ownership convention generalizes), and cairn/ruling (the module + thin bin/cmd wrapper layout, and CAIRN_ROOTS_PARENT as the proof's seam).
state_and_history: compiled to state.json + history.json beside this charter once its ticket exists — the charter-state-history split. Built under Akien's direct ratification the night of 2026-07-31, ahead of the workflow chain (the chain itself was the day's casualty); the ticket is filed edge (a), not a silent omission.
filed_edges: (a) NO TICKET YET — same shape as cairn/ruling's edge (a), same day, same reason; owes state/history sidecars when tickets resume.

(b) COMMAND OWNERSHIP IS A CONVENTION, NOT A SCHEMA: a charter owns `cairn <name>` iff its `invoke` (or a facility block's) mentions it. The gate enforces the convention, so an unowned command cannot pass silently — but nothing yet refuses a charter that mentions a command it does not actually implement. Schema field when the charter envelope lands (MAP.md Q6).

(c) THE PROVEME-CROSSING WIRING IS NOT DONE: the skill class's prove_gate now EXISTS and is runnable (`cairn cairnmap --gate`), but nothing fires it automatically when a skill node crosses PROVEME — that wiring belongs to the chokepoint and lands with the workflow chain, not here.
(d) ONE SOURCE, MANY SURFACES is half-built: the chat/CLI render exists (the design's own v0); the web-UI pane on the ONE web server is design-only until the server lands on the spine.

(e) the completeness scan covers skills (three-way), commands, and cairn/ package dirs; repo-root code outside those lanes (e.g. a new top-level tree) is only covered once it carries a charter — the scan cannot demand a charter from code it has no rule for finding.
gates: proof gate — proofs/test_cairnmap.py, runnable bare (python3) and under the tester. Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed (git). And it IS a gate: `--gate` is the skill node-class's prove_gate (node_classes/skill.json), the derivation gate that class has carried as a labeled IOU since 2026-07-15.
falsifier: RED, by physics, on any of: (1) a charter'd skill or component that does not appear in the root render (completeness, direction one); (2) an uncharted `bin/cmd/` entry that renders as a normal help line instead of a RED (direction two — an undocumented command must be impossible, not just unlabeled); (3) a skill carrying a charter but absent from `members_so_far` that does not red — the measured 2026-07-31 roster defect, replayed as a proof tooth; (4) an installed-skill symlink pointing away from its charter'd source that does not red; (5) a charter that fails to parse and is silently SKIPPED rather than loudly listed (the invisible-failure shape); (6) the surface containing prose that exists in no charter — authored help, the exact rot this replaces; (7) `--gate` exiting 0 while any red exists, or the plain render exiting non-zero because of one; (8) the render MUTATING anything (a view that writes is a device wearing a view's clothes); (9) standing in a chartered directory yielding the whole map instead of that component's brief.
proof: proofs/test_cairnmap.py — a synthetic two-root world via CAIRN_ROOTS_PARENT + CAIRN_SKILLS_INSTALL_DIR (the live tree is never read or written). NON-VACUITY FIRST: the consistent world is GREEN — gate exit 0, every charter rendered, every skill and command present — before any defect is introduced, so the reds cannot be the gate reddening unconditionally. Then each falsifier tooth: the roster omission replay, the roster entry with no charter, the dangling and the mis-aimed symlink, the uninstalled skill, the uncharted command, the corrupt charter (loud AND the rest still renders), code without a charter in the package, the detail brief from inside a directory, the unknown-name refusal, first-sentence truncation as a cut not a break, and the exit-code contract on both verbs.
owner: CC owns the render code (cairn/cairnmap/ + bin/cmd/cairnmap) and its proof, and gates writes to them. It owns NONE of what it renders: charters are owned by their components, the skill roster by node_classes/skill.json, the command set by bin/. That split is the ruling ('a view, not a device') stated as Law 6.
traces_to: Law 1 (an answered 'what can I do here' becomes structure — the resolver stops re-deriving the system's own shape from a stale map)
Law 5 (intent shares an address with code — this renders exactly that co-location, and could not exist without it)
Law 6 (it owns only the render; every rendered fact has its own owner elsewhere)
Law 7 (a red is loud in the surface itself; a presentation surface still presents)
Telos 1 ('explain what I can do' with the inference compiled out)
